meta.title: ERP readiness test | Cyrrus
meta.description: Ten questions to find out whether your company is ready to select an ERP: processes, data, team, budget and sponsorship. Instant result.

hero.title: Is your company ready for an ERP?
hero.description: Ten questions for the leadership committee, before opening a selection process. Three minutes, instant result and no data left behind.

intro.text: An ERP project depends on the software and on what the company has ready. This test measures five foundations Cyrrus reviews before a selection process and tells you which to close first.
bullets: Processes, data, team, budget and sponsorship: two questions for each.
Designed for CEOs, CFOs, COOs and leadership-committee members.
Indicative: ideally several executives answer it separately and compare.

quiz.title: Answer for how your company is today, not how you'd like it to be
quiz.disclaimer: Indicative guide built by Cyrrus from its experience. It is not a statistical study and does not replace a diagnosis.
quiz.ctaText: We can review the result with your committee and turn it into a plan before you select.

questions.text: Are your main processes (procure-to-pay, order-to-cash) documented and owned by someone?
options: They aren't documented; each person does them their own way
The people who run them know them, but nothing is written down
They are partly documented, with owners in some areas
They are documented, owned and measured with indicators

questions.text: How similar are processes across areas or sites?
options: Each area or site works differently
Some processes share common rules
They are nearly identical, with exceptions we know about
They are standardized, and exceptions are approved

questions.text: Where does customer, product and supplier information live today?
options: In spreadsheets and personal files
In several systems that aren't reconciled with each other
In a main system, with duplicates and inconsistencies
In a single clean source, with an owner

questions.text: How much do you trust the inventory and receivables figures you receive?
options: I check them by hand or rebuild them
I use them, but they usually change at close
They're reliable except in known spots
They're reliable and traceable to their source

questions.text: Are there business people (not just IT) who can give real time to the project?
options: Nobody can step away from operations
A few hours a week
Key people at half time
A dedicated team, with their usual work covered

questions.text: How did the company fare with previous system changes?
options: There were failed implementations and nothing was learned
They went live, but adoption was uneven
They were adopted well, without a formal change method
They were adopted with change management and usage was measured

questions.text: How has the project been budgeted?
options: There is no budget yet
With licenses only
With licenses and implementation
With the five-year total cost: licenses, implementation, integrations, internal team and contingency

questions.text: Are the business problem and the expected benefit clear?
options: Not clear; the aim is to "modernize"
There's a general idea of what to improve
There are qualitative goals
There are measurable goals with a baseline from today

questions.text: Who sponsors the project at senior leadership level?
options: Nobody is defined
IT drives it alone
An executive supports it, without giving it time
An executive sponsor and a committee that decides

questions.text: Are the area leaders aligned with the changes they will see in their processes?
options: They haven't been consulted or they oppose it
They have opinions, but there's no agreement
There's general agreement, without concrete commitments
They're aligned and co-accountable for results

bands.title: Not yet: start with the foundations
bands.summary: Selecting an ERP today would expose you to a project with risks you don't yet control. The gaps below are the recommended groundwork.

bands.title: Almost ready: close the gaps before buying
bands.summary: You have foundations to start, but some areas could derail the project. Working on the gaps below in parallel with defining requirements lets you reach selection with fewer risks.

bands.title: Ready to select
bands.summary: Your foundations allow you to open a selection process with clear criteria. Next comes defining requirements and comparing alternatives independently.

procesos.low: Document and standardize the processes that move the most money (procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, inventory, accounting close) before comparing systems. An ERP automates what exists: if the process is ambiguous, it scales the ambiguity.
procesos.mid: Close the exceptions: decide which differences between areas or sites are legitimate and which are habit. Every exception you keep is paid for in the implementation.

datos.low: Clean up the customer, product and supplier masters and name an owner for each. Data migration must be budgeted and have an owner.
datos.mid: Define the single source for each piece of data and measure duplicates before the project, not during it.

equipo.low: Define who will give real time: the key people in each area need time to define processes, validate configurations and test. Without them, the project is left in the vendor's hands.
equipo.mid: Formalize the time commitment by role and cover their usual tasks. Internal team time is a cost worth budgeting for.

presupuesto.low: Build the five-year total cost: licenses, implementation, infrastructure, integrations and internal time. A license quote is not a budget.
presupuesto.mid: Complete the budget with what's missing (integrations, data migration, training, contingency) and set benefit goals with a baseline.

patrocinio.low: Name a senior-leadership sponsor with the authority to decide and resolve conflicts between areas. A project driven only by IT becomes a technology project, not a business one.
patrocinio.mid: Turn support into a committee with decisions and dates, and align each area's leaders with the changes they will see in their processes.

items.question: How long does the test take?
items.answer: About three minutes. It has ten single-choice questions and the result appears at the end, with no sign-up.

items.question: Is my information stored?
items.answer: We don't ask for personal data. Answers are calculated in your browser and are not sent to Cyrrus. If you accepted analytics cookies, we only record that you completed the test and the result range.

items.question: Who should answer it?
items.answer: Ideally several members of the leadership committee (general management, finance, operations and IT), each on their own. The differences between their answers can be as revealing as the score.

items.question: What do I do with the result?
items.answer: Use it as a to-do list before selection. If you like, we review it with your committee and turn it into a plan with owners and dates.

meta.title: ERP total cost calculator | Cyrrus
meta.description: Calculate the total cost of an ERP over several years: licenses, implementation, integrations, internal team and contingency. Visible, editable assumptions.

hero.title: ERP total cost calculator
hero.description: A license quote is not a budget. Build the multi-year cost with the blocks a license quote leaves out, with visible and editable assumptions.

intro.text: The fields are empty on purpose: we don't use "typical" percentages because no verifiable primary source exists for them. Enter the figures from the proposals you have (ask each vendor for the breakdown). All figures use the same currency.
intro.example: Load the example with a published price
intro.exampleNote: The example loads only one public data point: Dynamics 365 Business Central Essentials, US$80 per user per month billed annually, and 25 users (list price published by Microsoft, checked in October 2026; it can vary by country and negotiation). Everything else stays at zero.

usuarios.label: Users
usuarios.hint: Full users who will use the system.

precioCloud.label: Subscription per user per month
precioCloud.hint: Take the value from your quote.

precioPerpetual.label: License per user (one-time)
precioPerpetual.hint: Take the value from your quote.

mantenimiento.label: Annual maintenance (% of the license)
mantenimiento.hint: Applies only to a perpetual license.

implPct.label: Implementation (% of the first-year license or subscription)
implPct.hint: Analysis, configuration, testing. Ask the implementation partner for the value.

integPct.label: Integrations and data migration (% of the same)
integPct.hint: E-invoicing, banks, other systems, master-data cleanup.

trainPct.label: Training and change management (% of implementation)
trainPct.hint: Ask whether it's included in the quote.

personas.label: Internal people dedicated to the project
personas.hint: Those who define processes, validate and test.

costoMes.label: Monthly cost per person
costoMes.hint: Salary and charges of an area leader.

dedicacion.label: Time given to the project (%)
dedicacion.hint: Share of their time taken from their usual work.

infra.label: Infrastructure, support and add-ons per year

contPct.label: Contingency (% of project costs)
contPct.hint: A margin for what wasn't foreseen.

results.title: Your total cost
results.share: The license or subscription is {{pct}}% of the total cost.
results.shareNote: The rest is what a license quote doesn't show.
results.note: The project is assumed to happen in year 1. Recurring costs repeat every year.
results.disclaimer: Indicative tool: not a quote, excludes taxes and benefits, and does not replace a business-case analysis.
results.ctaText: We can review the proposals you have on the table with you and build each one's comparable total cost.
results.empty: Enter your figures to see the total cost.
results.reference: A verifiable data point on budget risk: in Panorama Consulting's The 2026 ERP Report (170 organizations, January 2025 to January 2026), more than a quarter of projects went over budget and the most common cause was an unexpected need for additional technology.

items.question: Are there starting values or reference percentages?
items.answer: No. The fields are empty because we couldn't find a verifiable primary source for "typical" implementation, integration or maintenance percentages; industry guides give them as unsourced rules of thumb. The example button loads only a price published by a vendor (Business Central Essentials).

items.question: Is what I enter stored?
items.answer: No. Calculations run in your browser and are not sent to Cyrrus. If you accepted analytics cookies, we only record that you used the tool.

items.question: How do I use it to compare vendors?
items.answer: Ask each vendor for the same proposal, with the same scope and broken down by block, and load each one separately. Compare the total cost, not the license.

items.question: What does it leave out?
items.answer: It leaves out taxes, financing and the project's benefits (savings, revenue, risk reduction). It covers only the cost side.
